description: This talk, by Raya Saraireh, tells the story of a brief but deeply meaningful six-month friendship that unexpectedly shaped her life. After losing a close friend who encouraged her to pursue self-improvement and overcome her fear of public speaking, she experienced grief, loneliness, and self-doubt. Over time, she transformed that pain into motivation, rebuilding herself through fitness, new friendships, and eventually public speaking. The talk reflects on how even short-lived relationships can leave permanent emotional impact, showing that what is lost can still guide who we become. Raya Saraireh is an 8th grade iCademy student. She is extremely passionate about music and writing; she spends most of her free time writing lyrics. Her speech invites viewers to see the good in something horrible, that a painful loss can lead to growth. She speaks about losing her closest friend and how the disdain, though first felt painful and melancholic, transformed her into becoming who she is today

Through these objects, she introduces the idea of “ephemeral permanence,” showing how short-lived experiences can leave lasting emotional impact. The talk ultimately reminds us that the smallest, most ordinary moments are often the ones that stay with us the longest. Aiza Mulla is a 10th grade student and TEDx speaker at iCademy Middle East. In her speech, "A Memory Box," she will explore how small, meaningful objects like tickets, notes, photos, and childhood keepsakes can hold powerful memories. title: When History Ends but Identity Does Not | Kar Nursali | TEDxiCademy Youth

Inspired by Eleanor Roosevelt’s words, Aleena explains that pain doesn’t have to hold us back. It can become the foundation for growth, resilience, and purpose. Her message encourages others to turn their struggles into stepping-stones rather than stumbling blocks. Aleena Mobeen is an 8th grade student and a TEDx speaker at iCademy, who likes piano, art, and most importantly: public speaking. Her speech "Pain as a Building Block" will reflect on how a short moment of pain can change you forever, and how you can use pain to build yourself. This is how we find our best selves. Through Matt’s 20 + years experience as an NRL Head Coach, his relentless pursuit was to discover how to merge wellbeing with high performance for his team.

description:
Why do some children grow up believing they are not intelligent simply because they learn differently?

In this TEDx talk, Dr. Vini Jhariya explores the silent struggle of children who are misunderstood in classrooms and at home. Often labeled as distracted, careless, or “not trying hard enough,” many children spend years hiding their confusion instead of receiving support.

Drawing from both personal experience and years of working with children, she speaks about dyslexia, learning differences, and the emotional impact of being constantly misunderstood during childhood.

Rather than asking why some children cannot fit into the system, this talk challenges us to ask whether the system truly understands every child.

This is a conversation about learning, identity, and the power of being seen before it is too late. Dr. Vini Jhariya is a Child and Clinical Psychologist with over 12 years of experience in neurodevelopmental and mental health care. She serves as the Director of Urjasvini
title: The Labels That Shape Childhood | Dr. Vini Jhariya | TEDxMotilal Nehru College

description:
What if overthinking is not a flaw… but a survival instinct?

In this powerful TEDx talk, Kamaljeet challenges one of the most misunderstood traits of the modern mind. Blending neuroscience, evolution, personal stories, philosophy, and real-life experiences from risk management and law, he explores how the very habit we call “overthinking” may actually be humanity’s oldest survival tool.

From sleepless nights before a simple picnic to uncovering hidden financial fraud during a high-stakes acquisition, this talk reveals the difference between an untrained mind trapped in anxiety and a trained mind capable of foresight, preparedness, and strategic thinking.

Through stories ranging from Arjuna in the Bhagavad Gita to Apollo 13, Japan’s disaster preparedness, and Steve Jobs’ leadership, the talk reframes fear, stress, and mental spirals as raw mental energy waiting to be directed.

This is not a talk about eliminating overthinking.

Through powerful stories, thought-provoking insights, and lessons drawn from individuals and nations that chose transformation over limitation, this talk reveals that lasting change begins when someone decides to take responsibility for their future. description:
¿Qué pasaría si el mayor poder de una organización fuera algo que no se puede ver?. 
En esta charla, Rodrigo Fernández de Paredes explora cómo las experiencias humanas transforman culturas, inspiran liderazgo y crean conexiones reales entre las personas y las marcas. Porque las experiencias que más nos marcan nacen de pequeños gestos, conversaciones y decisiones del día a día. Rodrigo Fernández de Paredes es especialista en experiencia del cliente, liderazgo y transformación organizacional. A lo largo de su trayectoria, ha trabajado impulsando culturas centradas en las personas, demostrando cómo las experiencias humanas pueden fortalecer marcas, equipos y organizaciones. En su charla “El poder invisible de la experiencia”, comparte reflexiones sobre el impacto que tienen los pequeños gestos, las conversaciones y las decisiones cotidianas en la forma en que conectamos y generamos cambio.
